# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yan_2026_mirtazapine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yan_2026_mirtazapine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S601238>

Yan and colleagues fitted a one-compartment model with first-order absorption
to 210 routine therapeutic-drug-monitoring (TDM) serum concentrations of
mirtazapine from 105 Chinese inpatients with depression. Almost every sample
was drawn about 12 h after the nightly dose, so the absorption rate constant
was not identifiable and was fixed at 1.2 1/h from a published analysis
(Grasmader 2004). Three binary covariates were retained on apparent oral
clearance, combined multiplicatively:

$$CL/F = 28.9 \times (1 - 0.294\,BMI) \times (1 - 0.269\,PRX) \times (1 - 0.511\,FLV)$$

where BMI is 1 for BMI >= 28 kg/m^2, PRX is concomitant paroxetine and FLV is
concomitant fluvoxamine; V/F is 310 L. In the packaged model these are the
canonical columns `DIS_OBESE`, `CONMED_PAROXETINE` and `CONMED_FLUVOXAMINE`.

```{r load-model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yan_2026_mirtazapine"))
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical-value and fixed-eta solves have no omega to sample from; rxode2
# says so with a warning that carries no information here, so only that
# message is muffled.
solve_fixed <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
```

# Population

105 inpatients (43 men, 62 women; age 13-79 years, mean 48.5) of Chinese
ethnicity with depressive disorders were treated with 7.5-45 mg mirtazapine
tablets once nightly at The Affiliated Brain Hospital of Guangzhou Medical
University between May 2024 and September 2025 (Methods; Table 1). Mean body
weight was 62.2 kg (25.4-104.0) and 20 patients (19%) had BMI >= 28 kg/m^2.
Concomitant antidepressants and antipsychotics were common: venlafaxine 26,
paroxetine 13, duloxetine 12, risperidone 10, fluvoxamine 6 and fluoxetine 5
patients. Patients with severe hepatic disease or eGFR below
30 mL/min/1.73 m^2 were excluded, and no smokers were included.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yan_2026_mirtazapine"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Element | Value in model | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: one compartment, first-order absorption | `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)` | Methods, Data Analysis (NONMEM ADVAN2) |
| `lka` | `fixed(log(1.2))` 1/h | Methods, Base Model; Table 2 'Ka 1.2 FIX' |
| `lcl` | `log(28.9)` L/h | Table 2; Results CL/F equation |
| `lvc` | `log(310)` L | Table 2; Results V/F equation |
| `e_obese_cl` | -0.294 | Table 2 'Theta CL-BMI'; Results CL/F equation |
| `e_par_cl` | -0.269 | Table 2 'Theta CL-Paroxetine'; Results CL/F equation |
| `e_fluvox_cl` | -0.511 | Table 2 'Theta CL-Fluvoxamine'; Results CL/F equation |
| Covariate form `(1 + theta * COV)` | multiplicative product on CL/F | Methods, Covariate Model; Results CL/F equation |
| `etalcl` | variance 0.0613 | Table 2, IIV column for CL/F |
| `etalvc` | variance 0.131 | Table 2, IIV column for V/F |
| `propSd` | `sqrt(0.0747)` | Table 2 'PRO'; Methods, proportional error model |
| BMI coding (1 = BMI >= 28 kg/m^2) | `DIS_OBESE` | Methods, Covariate Model |
| Concentration units ng/mL | `Cc <- 1000 * central / vc` | Table 1; Methods (therapeutic range 30-80 ng/mL) |

# Structural check against the closed form

A one-compartment model with first-order absorption has a closed-form
steady-state concentration. Solving the packaged model for the typical
patient of each subgroup and comparing against that closed form, built from
the printed parameters only, confirms the covariate products, the unit
conversion and the absorption rate.

```{r closed-form}
subgroups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,                       ~DIS_OBESE, ~CONMED_PAROXETINE, ~CONMED_FLUVOXAMINE,
  "None",                       0,          0,                  0,
  "BMI >= 28",                  1,          0,                  0,
  "Paroxetine",                 0,          1,                  0,
  "Fluvoxamine",                0,          0,                  1,
  "BMI >= 28 + paroxetine",     1,          1,                  0,
  "BMI >= 28 + fluvoxamine",    1,          0,                  1
) |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = group),
    # Results CL/F equation, written out from the printed numbers
    cl_paper = 28.9 * (1 - 0.294 * DIS_OBESE) * (1 - 0.269 * CONMED_PAROXETINE) *
      (1 - 0.511 * CONMED_FLUVOXAMINE)
  )

# Steady-state concentration t hours after a once-daily dose, ng/mL per mg
css_closed <- function(t, cl, v = 310, ka = 1.2, tau = 24) {
  k <- cl / v
  1000 * ka / (v * (ka - k)) *
    (exp(-k * t) / (1 - exp(-k * tau)) - exp(-ka * t) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau)))
}

ss_events <- function(covs, obs_times) {
  covs <- mutate(covs, id = seq_len(n()))
  dose <- mutate(covs, time = 0, amt = 1, evid = 1L, ss = 1L, ii = 24, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(covs, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, ss = 0L, ii = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

ev_typ <- ss_events(select(subgroups, -cl_paper), obs_times = c(11, 12))
sim_typ <- solve_fixed(
  mod_typical,
  events = ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  left_join(mutate(subgroups, id = seq_len(n())) |> select(id, group, cl_paper), by = "id") |>
  mutate(closed = css_closed(time, cl_paper), rel_err = Cc / closed - 1)

# Same parameters on both sides, so the difference is pure integrator error.
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_typ$rel_err)) < 1e-6)

sim_typ |>
  select(group, time, Cc, closed) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Subgroup" = group, "Hours post-dose" = time,
    "Model (ng/mL per mg)" = Cc, "Closed form (ng/mL per mg)" = closed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Typical steady-state concentration per mg of daily dose.")
```

# Replicate Figure 6: dose versus typical steady-state concentration

Figure 6 of Yan 2026 plots the steady-state concentration of each subgroup
against the daily dose. The plotted points coincide with the model's typical
value **11 h** after the dose, not 12 h (the paper describes a 20:00 dose and
an 08:00 sample); see Assumptions and deviations. The comparison below uses the
45 mg end points, digitised by the maintainers from Figure 6.

```{r figure-6}
doses <- c(7.5, 15, 22.5, 30, 37.5, 45)
fig6 <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time == 11) |>
  select(group, Cc) |>
  tidyr::crossing(dose = doses) |>
  mutate(conc = Cc * dose)

ggplot(fig6, aes(dose, conc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(30, 80), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 160, colour = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Daily dose (mg/d)", y = "Typical steady-state concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Yan 2026 (typical value 11 h post-dose)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Figure 6, 45 mg points, digitised by the maintainers (+/- about 3 ng/mL).
fig6_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,                    ~published,
  "None",                    63,
  "BMI >= 28",               97,
  "Paroxetine",              92,
  "Fluvoxamine",             137,
  "BMI >= 28 + paroxetine",  130,
  "BMI >= 28 + fluvoxamine", 197
)
fig6_cmp <- fig6 |>
  filter(dose == 45) |>
  mutate(group = as.character(group)) |>
  inner_join(fig6_digitised, by = "group") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (conc / published - 1))

# Typical values against digitised points: limited by the digitisation, not
# by the model; a wrong covariate effect or unit moves a row by >= 25%.
stopifnot(nrow(fig6_cmp) == 6, max(abs(fig6_cmp$pct_diff)) < 6)

fig6_cmp |>
  select(group, conc, published, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Subgroup" = group, "Model, 45 mg (ng/mL)" = conc,
    "Figure 6, digitised (ng/mL)" = published, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Replicate Figure 5: probability of target attainment

The paper's Monte Carlo simulation (1000 virtual patients per subgroup and
dose) reports the percentage of steady-state concentrations inside the
30-80 ng/mL therapeutic window. Because the model is linear in dose, the
attainment can be computed without Monte Carlo noise: the packaged model is
solved on a 12 x 12 Gauss-Hermite grid over the two random effects at 1 mg,
scaled to each dose, and the proportional residual error is integrated
analytically. This gives the model's exact attainment, so it can be compared
tightly against the paper's numbers.

The same calculation is repeated with the alternative reading of Table 2, in
which the IIV and PRO entries are standard deviations rather than variances.

```{r pta-grid}
gauss_hermite <- function(n) {
  # Golub-Welsch nodes and weights for the physicists' weight exp(-x^2)
  j <- matrix(0, n, n)
  off <- sqrt(seq_len(n - 1) / 2)
  j[cbind(1:(n - 1), 2:n)] <- off
  j[cbind(2:n, 1:(n - 1))] <- off
  e <- eigen(j, symmetric = TRUE)
  list(x = e$values, w = sqrt(pi) * e$vectors[1, ]^2)
}

pta_exact <- function(omega2_cl, omega2_v, sigma2, obs_time) {
  gh <- gauss_hermite(12)
  # Standard-normal nodes z = sqrt(2) * x with weights w / sqrt(pi)
  grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    i = seq_along(gh$x), j = seq_along(gh$x)
  ) |>
    mutate(
      etalcl = sqrt(2 * omega2_cl) * gh$x[i],
      etalvc = sqrt(2 * omega2_v) * gh$x[j],
      w = gh$w[i] * gh$w[j] / pi
    )
  covs <- tidyr::crossing(select(subgroups, -cl_paper), node = seq_len(nrow(grid)))
  ev <- ss_events(select(covs, -node), obs_times = obs_time)
  params <- covs |>
    mutate(id = seq_len(n())) |>
    left_join(mutate(grid, node = seq_len(n())), by = "node") |>
    select(id, etalcl, etalvc)
  sim <- solve_fixed(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "sigma"),
    events = ev, params = params, returnType = "data.frame",
    rtol = 1e-8, atol = 1e-10, ssRtol = 1e-8, ssAtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6
  )
  sim |>
    left_join(mutate(covs, id = seq_len(n())) |> select(id, group, node), by = "id") |>
    left_join(mutate(grid, node = seq_len(n())) |> select(node, w), by = "node") |>
    tidyr::crossing(dose = doses) |>
    mutate(
      conc = Cc * dose,
      p_in = pnorm((80 / conc - 1) / sqrt(sigma2)) - pnorm((30 / conc - 1) / sqrt(sigma2))
    ) |>
    group_by(group, dose) |>
    summarise(pta = 100 * sum(w * p_in), wsum = sum(w), .groups = "drop")
}

pta_var_11 <- pta_exact(0.0613, 0.131, 0.0747, obs_time = 11)
pta_var_12 <- pta_exact(0.0613, 0.131, 0.0747, obs_time = 12)
pta_sd_11 <- pta_exact(0.0613^2, 0.131^2, 0.0747^2, obs_time = 11)
stopifnot(all(abs(pta_var_11$wsum - 1) < 1e-10))
```

```{r pta-compare}
# Attainment percentages quoted in the Results text for Figure 5.
pta_published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,                    ~dose, ~published,
  "None",                    15,    16.0,
  "None",                    30,    70.0,
  "None",                    37.5,  74.6,
  "None",                    45,    66.5,
  "BMI >= 28",               15,    48.8,
  "Paroxetine",              15,    45.9,
  "Fluvoxamine",             15,    78.4,
  "BMI >= 28 + paroxetine",  15,    76.5,
  "BMI >= 28 + fluvoxamine", 15,    69.8,
  "BMI >= 28 + fluvoxamine", 37.5,  4.7,
  "BMI >= 28 + fluvoxamine", 45,    2.0
)

pta_cmp <- pta_published |>
  left_join(
    mutate(pta_var_11, group = as.character(group)) |> select(group, dose, var_11 = pta),
    by = c("group", "dose")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    mutate(pta_var_12, group = as.character(group)) |> select(group, dose, var_12 = pta),
    by = c("group", "dose")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    mutate(pta_sd_11, group = as.character(group)) |> select(group, dose, sd_11 = pta),
    by = c("group", "dose")
  )

# The model values are exact (no Monte Carlo); the paper's are from 1000
# simulated patients, a binomial SE of at most 1.6 points. A 4-point bound is
# 2.5 SE; the SD reading misses the first row alone by about 10 points.
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(pta_cmp$var_11),
  max(abs(pta_cmp$var_11 - pta_cmp$published)) < 4,
  median(abs(pta_cmp$sd_11 - pta_cmp$published)) > 5
)

pta_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Subgroup" = group, "Dose (mg/d)" = dose, "Published PTA (%)" = published,
    "Model, 11 h (%)" = var_11, "Model, 12 h (%)" = var_12,
    "SD reading, 11 h (%)" = sd_11
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Probability of 30-80 ng/mL attainment: Yan 2026 Results (Figure 5) against the packaged model.")
```

```{r pta-plot}
ggplot(pta_var_11, aes(dose, pta, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "Daily dose (mg/d)", y = "Concentrations within 30-80 ng/mL (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the Figure 5 inset panels of Yan 2026 (exact, 11 h post-dose)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Replicate Figure 4: stochastic prediction interval by dose

Figure 4 compares external observations with the 95% prediction interval of
simulated steady-state concentrations for patients without covariates. The
simulation below draws 200 virtual patients per dose with between-subject
and residual variability, sampled 11 h after the nightly dose (the sampling
time that reproduces Figures 5 and 6; see Assumptions and deviations).

```{r figure-4}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260603)
n_per_dose <- 200
covs4 <- tibble::tibble(
  dose_mg = rep(doses, each = n_per_dose),
  DIS_OBESE = 0, CONMED_PAROXETINE = 0, CONMED_FLUVOXAMINE = 0
) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
ev4 <- bind_rows(
  mutate(covs4, time = 0, amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L, ss = 1L, ii = 24, cmt = "depot"),
  mutate(covs4, time = 11, amt = 0, evid = 0L, ss = 0L, ii = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev4, returnType = "data.frame", maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  left_join(select(covs4, id, dose_mg), by = "id")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim4$sim))

fig4 <- sim4 |>
  group_by(dose_mg) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(sim, 0.025), med = median(sim), hi = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(fig4, aes(dose_mg)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 3, colour = "red") +
  geom_point(aes(y = med), colour = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Daily dose (mg/d)", y = "Steady-state concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates the prediction intervals of Figure 4 of Yan 2026 (median and 95% PI)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Figure 4 medians digitised by the maintainers (+/- about 2 ng/mL).
fig4_digitised <- tibble::tibble(dose_mg = doses, published = c(9, 19, 30, 40, 49, 57))
fig4_cmp <- inner_join(fig4, fig4_digitised, by = "dose_mg") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (med / published - 1))

# Cohort medians (200 patients, SE about 3%): assert on the centre only.
stopifnot(abs(median(fig4_cmp$pct_diff)) < 10)

fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg/d)" = dose_mg, "2.5th pct" = lo, "Median" = med, "97.5th pct" = hi,
    "Figure 4 median, digitised" = published, "Median difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA values. Steady-state NCA on the typical patient of
each subgroup (30 mg once daily for 15 days, rich sampling over the last
dosing interval) is compared against the closed-form values implied by the
printed parameters: AUC over the interval equals dose / (CL/F), and the trough
follows from the closed-form steady-state profile.

```{r pknca}
nca_covs <- select(subgroups, -cl_paper) |> mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
nca_dose <- tidyr::crossing(nca_covs, time = seq(0, 14 * 24, by = 24)) |>
  mutate(amt = 30, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
nca_obs <- tidyr::crossing(nca_covs, time = c(0, seq(14 * 24, 15 * 24, by = 0.25))) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
nca_ev <- bind_rows(nca_dose, nca_obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

nca_sim <- solve_fixed(
  mod_typical,
  events = nca_ev, returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  left_join(select(nca_covs, id, group), by = "id") |>
  mutate(group = as.character(group))

conc_df <- nca_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, group, time, Cc)
dose_df <- nca_dose |>
  mutate(group = as.character(group)) |>
  select(id, group, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | group + id,
  concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h"
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 14 * 24, end = 15 * 24,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_reference <- subgroups |>
  mutate(
    group = as.character(group),
    auclast = 1000 * 30 / cl_paper,
    cav = auclast / 24,
    cmin = 30 * css_closed(24, cl_paper)
  ) |>
  select(group, auclast, cav, cmin)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = nca_reference,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", cav = "ng/mL", cmin = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-patient steady-state NCA (30 mg once daily) against the closed form. * differs by >20%.")

nca_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cav", "cmin")) |>
  select(group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(nca_reference, -group, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("group", "PPTESTCD")
  )
# Deterministic: the residual is the trapezoid error on a 15-min grid and the
# 15-day approach to steady state (>99.99% for the slowest subgroup).
stopifnot(nrow(nca_long) == 18, max(abs(nca_long$PPORRES / nca_long$ref - 1)) < 0.01)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV and residual-error magnitudes are read as variances.** Table 2 prints
  an "IIV" column (0.0613 for CL/F, 0.131 for V/F) and a "PRO" row (0.0747)
  without saying whether these are variances or standard deviations. The
  Methods define both random effects through their variances (omega^2,
  sigma^2), and with all three read as variances the packaged model reproduces
  every attainment percentage the Results quote for Figure 5 to within about
  1 percentage point; the standard-deviation reading misses most of
  them by tens of points (table above). The model therefore uses `etalcl ~ 0.0613`,
  `etalvc ~ 0.131` and `propSd = sqrt(0.0747) = 0.273`.
* **Abstract versus Results values.** The abstract gives CL/F 29.3 L/h and V/F
  348 L; Table 2 and the printed final-model equations give 28.9 L/h and
  310 L. The model uses Table 2, which is also what reproduces Figures 5 and 6.
* **Simulation sampling time.** The paper simulates a 20:00 dose with an 08:00
  sample (12 h). The plotted Figure 6 values, the Figure 5 attainment
  percentages and the Figure 4 medians all match the model's steady-state
  concentration 11 h after the dose, not 12 h (the 12 h attainment column
  above misses by up to 7 points). The figure replications therefore sample
  at 11 h; the model itself is unaffected.
* **Ka unit.** Table 2 labels Ka as 'L/h'; it is a rate constant in 1/h, as the
  Methods state.
* **BMI covariate.** The paper's BMI covariate is a dichotomy at 28 kg/m^2 (the
  Chinese adult obesity cut-off), encoded here as the canonical obesity
  indicator `DIS_OBESE`; the continuous BMI is not used. Users applying the
  model elsewhere should derive `DIS_OBESE` with the same 28 kg/m^2 threshold.
* **Covariate scope.** Fluvoxamine was taken by only 6 patients, so its 51.1%
  effect is imprecise (the paper notes this). Smokers were not studied, so the
  model carries no CYP1A2-induction effect.
* **Supplement.** The supplementary document holds the covariate-screening
  steps (Supplementary Tables 1-3) and the literature data used for external
  evaluation (Supplementary Table 4); it carries no model parameters. The
  screened-but-dropped covariates are listed in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* No erratum or correction was found for this article (Europe PMC search,
  2026-11-13).
